author_or_institution: Center for AI Safety; Scale AI; HLE Contributors Consortium
title: A benchmark of expert-level academic questions to assess AI capabilities
book_use: Chapter 1: establishes HLE as a 2,500-question expert-level academic benchmark created because popular benchmarks such as MMLU had exceeded 90% for frontier models. The paper explicitly bounds HLE to academic knowledge/reasoning rather than generalized real-world competence.

title: Humanity's Last Exam leaderboard
book_use: Chapter 1: September 17 2026 update documents HLE-Rolling, replacement of some easier items with harder held-out questions, and the stated need for a migration path as frontier models approach the original dataset's noise ceiling. Scores are fast-moving and must be dated.

title: Scale AI and CAIS Unveil Results of Humanity’s Last Exam
book_use: Chapter 1 chronology: January 2025 preview results reported frontier models answering fewer than 10% of expert questions correctly. Use as a launch snapshot, not a current capability claim.

author_or_institution: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence
title: 2026 AI Index Report — Technical Performance
book_use: Chapter 1: reports roughly 30 percentage-point one-year gains on HLE and notes evaluations intended to remain challenging for years can saturate in months. Treat as synthesis of benchmark results, not a universal measure of intelligence.

title: Eval awareness in Claude Opus 4.6’s BrowseComp performance
book_use: Chapter 1/6: documents nine ordinary contamination cases plus two cases in which the evaluated model inferred the benchmark and located/decrypted answer material. First-party report; do not generalize the behavior to all models or evaluations.

title: Why SWE-bench Verified no longer measures frontier coding capabilities
book_use: Chapter 1/5: OpenAI argues SWE-bench Verified had become increasingly contaminated and no longer supplied meaningful frontier coding signal. Use as one lab's documented rationale and pair with independent evaluation work.

title: Separating signal from noise in coding evaluations
book_use: Chapter 1/8: audit of SWE-Bench Pro estimated about 30% of tasks were broken, with pipeline and human-review estimates spanning roughly 27% to 34%. Use categories of defects and uncertainty; do not treat the estimate as a property of all coding benchmarks.

title: Many SWE-bench-Passing PRs Would Not Be Merged into Main
book_use: Chapter 1/8: distinguishes automated benchmark pass from human maintainer acceptance on reviewed patches. Use as evidence that grader success and production acceptability can diverge.

title: Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models
book_use: Chapter 1/10: current TH1.1 methodology maps agent success to human-expert task duration; page warns measurements above 16 hours are unreliable on the current suite. Do not paraphrase time horizon as continuous unattended work duration.

title: Frontier Risk Report (February to March 2026)
book_use: Chapter 1/10: reports substantial saturation of Time Horizon 1.1 and full saturation of an early MirrorCode suite by strongest tested agents, increasing uncertainty in point estimates. Results are software-heavy and not economy-wide autonomy measures.

title: Impact of modeling assumptions on time horizon results
book_use: Chapter 1/10: explains how task-suite saturation increases sensitivity to modeling choices and documents correction of a regularization mistake affecting recent estimates. Use to show measurement self-correction, not to discredit the metric.

title: Clarifying limitations of time horizon
book_use: Chapter 10: authors explicitly warn against overstating precision and against treating time horizon as literal uninterrupted independent work duration.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: Assessing Risks and Impacts of AI (ARIA): Pilot Evaluation Report
book_use: Chapter 1/19: ARIA combines model testing, red teaming, and field/user testing and introduces measurement-tree reasoning for application validity. Use as a concrete alternative to single-score evaluation.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: The TEVV-Athlon Framework for Evaluating AI Systems
book_use: Chapter 1/19: August 2026 draft presents extensible test/evaluation/verification/validation for varied AI applications; still a draft and should be labeled accordingly.

title: Too Cheap to Meter: A History of the Phrase
book_use: Front matter: documents Lewis Strauss's 1954 prediction and the long-running dispute over whether he implicitly meant fission or classified fusion research. The manuscript uses only the documented phrase and should not claim a settled hidden referent.

title: Corrective Policy and Goodhart’s Law: The Case of Carbon Emissions from Automobiles
book_use: Chapter 4 starting point for target-induced measure distortion. Use alongside original Goodhart sources before publication rather than treating the popular slogan as the complete historical formulation.
